summary.intent: Push three local commits (tests, docs and changeset, lint fixes) ending at 4c59ef11 to the remote branch perf/checker-extract-speed in the caliper repo using --no-verify, then link the trail and write a PR body.
summary.outcome: The push never landed; the remote stayed at 854da4c6. The assistant verified that 4c59ef11 exists, descends from the remote tip and would fast-forward cleanly, but it was blocked from pushing with --no-verify and the user's attempts did not take effect or return output. The user was told to run the push from a regular terminal.

repo: The speed commits live on the local branch perf/checker-extract-speed; the worktree-agent-aed2d... branch points at main's tip, so pushing it was rejected.
The follow-up branch perf/checker-shared-bases contains 4c59ef11, so it is based on the speed work.
The 3 commits to push (tests, docs and changeset, lint fixes) sit on top of remote tip 854da4c6, so the push is a clean fast-forward and cannot overwrite anything.
workflow: Verify a remote push with `git ls-remote origin <branch>` and confirm a commit's validity with `git cat-file -t` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before claiming where it lives.
The permission classifier blocks `git push --no-verify` from the assistant even when the user authorizes it in chat; the user has to run it themselves in a terminal.
User messages beginning with `!` arrived as plain text in this session, so the shell passthrough did not run and no command output reached the assistant.
When asking a user to run a command, ask them to paste the exact output so the next step rests on facts rather than guesses.
